title: Relative major and minor
summary: Every major key has a minor key that shares all its notes.

steps.title: Relative minor
steps.body:
A natural minor and C major use exactly the same notes, so they are relatives: A minor is the **relative minor** of C major. Every major key has one. It starts on the major key's 6th scale degree, 3 half steps below the tonic.

**Why it matters:** Relative keys share a key signature, so one sharp could mean G major or E minor. Lots of songs move between the two.

steps.title: Relative major
steps.body:
Going the other way, C major is the **relative major** of A minor: 3 half steps up from the minor tonic.

**Why it matters:** If a song in a minor key brightens up halfway through, it has often moved to its relative major.

steps.title: G major and E minor
steps.body: The same seven notes, with one sharp. G is the tonic of one, E of the other.

items.prompt: Play the E natural minor scale: the same notes, starting on E.

steps.title: Find the relative
steps.body: Pick any major key, count down 3 half steps, and play the natural minor scale from there. Check that it uses the same black keys.

items.prompt: What is the relative minor of G major?
What is the relative major of D minor?
What is the relative minor of F major?
